newsitem.title: USA: US tax ruling may mean millions for foreign firms.
newsitem.headline: US tax ruling may mean millions for foreign firms.

text.p: Foreign insurance firms with branch operations in the United States could be eligible for millions of dollars in tax refunds as a result of a court ruling in favor of a Canadian company, a lawyer involved with the case said Tuesday.

The U.S. Tax Court ruled against the way the Internal Revenue Service assessed taxes on branch operations in a case brought by North West Life Assurance of Canada, said Jerome Libin, an attorney with Sutherland, Asbill and Brennan, which represented North West Life in the case.

The court ruled that the way the IRS calculated investment income violated a tax treaty between the United States and Canada and that the treaty took precedent over the U.S. tax code, Libin said. The ruling, which affects foreign insurance firms with U.S. branch operations rather than separate subsidiaries, could mean hundreds of millions of dollars in tax refund claims, Libin said.

The IRS assessed tax liability on branch operations based on actual investment income or on the average amount earned by comparable U.S. insurance comapnies, whichever was greater. The tax treaty required assessments be based on actual income performance, Libin said.
The IRS could appeal the court decision, but a spokesman said it was too early to say what course of action the agency will take.

Libin said the North West case could set a precedent for another case involving branch operations of foreign banks. That case brought by National Westminster Bank Plc involves similar language in a tax treaty between the United States and the United Kingdom, he said.
